title: Let the model know the project
prompt:
# Story 5: Let the model know the project

- **Story**: XXX-enabler-project-context
- **Created**: 2026-11-08
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: draft an enabler in a project that has ADRs, principles, and other enablers, and read in the draft that it follows the template,
  names the ADRs it implements, and does not repeat what another enabler already covers.

## Story

As a team member, I want the AI to know the decisions, the principles, the practices and the work already described in my project, so that
the enabler it drafts fits them and does not contradict or repeat them.

## Acceptance tests

What the model is given (checked on the request a fake backend receives)

- [ ] **Given** a request for a draft, **Then** the first user message has a stable **project context**, then a cache point, then the
  **request**.
- [ ] **Given** the context, **Then** it has, in this order: "# Project context" and "Project: <name>"; "## Architecture decision records
  (read-only)" with the full Markdown of **every** ADR of the project, whatever its status, joined by "---"; "## Links between documents"
  (one line per enabler and story: what it derives from and what it links to, by label); "## Scope of the stories and architectural
  enablers" (the scope of each enabler, and the statement and the out of scope of each story); "## Principles of the team" (name and text of
  the principles that have text, or "None written yet"); and "## Practices of the team (fixed)" (the practices as text, with the
  non-negotiable ones marked).
- [ ] **Given** the context, **Then** it does **not** have the drivers (a driver reaches the model only when the user links it), and it does
  **not** have the architecture of the system (that goes with stories only).
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** it has "Document type: architectural enabler", "Assigned identifier: AE-0003", "Today's date:
  <date>", "## Derives from (ADRs)" (labels), the linked documents in full, "## Existing architectural enablers" (labels, or "- None"),
  "## Existing stories" (labels, or "- None") and "## Description" with the user's text. Repeated blank lines are collapsed.
- [ ] **Given** a document that is longer than 12,000 characters, **Then** it is cut there and ends with "[...cut: the document is longer]".
- [ ] **Given** the same project and the same links, **When** the user asks twice, **Then** the context block is identical, so that the
  second request reads it from the prompt cache. **Given** a new enabler or a changed ADR, **Then** the block changes.
- [ ] **Given** the system prompt, **Then** it asks for one Markdown document with no introduction, no closing remark and no code fence, and
  gives the template of an architectural enabler (below).

What the draft is like (checked by reading drafts from a real model; they are not automated)

- [ ] **Given** a draft, **Then** it follows the template: the title `# AE-0003. <short noun phrase>`; the lines Status (Proposed), Created
  (today's date), Completed (empty) and "Implements ADR(s)" with the number and title of each chosen ADR; and the sections Goal, Scope (In
  scope and Out of scope), Tasks and Definition of done.
- [ ] **Given** a draft, **Then** its Goal refers to the decision of the ADR it implements, its tasks are small steps in the order they are
  done, and its Definition of done has statements that a command, a test or an inspection can verify.
- [ ] **Given** a request that conflicts with an Accepted ADR, **Then** the draft leaves that part out and names it under Out of scope.
- [ ] **Given** an enabler that already covers part of the request, **Then** the draft does not repeat it and does not take it over.
- [ ] **Given** a non-negotiable practice, **Then** the draft does not contradict it, and cites it in brackets when a rule comes from it, for
  example (Practice: Ten-Minute Build) or (ADR 0006).
- [ ] **Given** a draft, **Then** it invents no numbers, names or technologies: what is missing is stated as the smallest reasonable
  assumption.

## Business rules and constraints

- **Stable first, dynamic after.** The context block changes only when an ADR, a link, a scope, a principle or the practices change. What
  changes with each request (identifier, date, links, the user's text) comes after the cache point.
- The context is the same for every kind of request about stories and enablers. It is sent only to the draft, the revision and (later) the
  edit of a story or enabler. The assistants of drivers, ADRs, principles and the architecture have their own, smaller context.
- Drivers are linked by the user, never sent on their own.
- The practices and the principles come from their own pages (`story-practices-tab.md`, `story-principles-and-practices.md`).

## Out of scope

- Checking that a draft is right. The user reviews it, as the practice "Pair programming" says.
- The prompt for stories, and the rules about layers (the architecture).
- Choosing or tuning the model, and the cost of tokens (Settings).

## Tasks

- [ ] Build the project context from the ADRs, the links, the scopes, the principles and the practices, in a fixed order.
- [ ] Build the request text with the lists of enablers and stories, and cut long documents at 12,000 characters.
- [ ] Write the system prompt for enablers with its template, and the rules on ADRs, practices, scope and assumptions (the Reference has the
  spike's text and what to split).
- [ ] Test the two builders: the exact text for a small project, the blank-line rule, the cut, and that the context is the same twice and
  different after a change.
- [ ] Read ten drafts from the real model for different prompts and ADRs, and fix the system prompt until they follow the checklist above.

tasks.text: Define and implement the context-block builder: assemble ADRs (all statuses, joined by `---`), links, scopes, principles and practices in the fixed order, and verify the output is identical across two calls with the same project state

Define and implement the request-block builder: identifier, date, ADR labels, linked documents (with the 12,000-character cut and the `[...cut: the document is longer]` suffix), enabler list, story list, and description, collapsing repeated blank lines

Write the system prompt for architectural enablers: output rules (one Markdown document, no preamble, no code fence), the enabler template, and the rules on Accepted ADRs, non-negotiable practices, existing scope, and assumptions
Wire the context block and the request block into the existing draft endpoint so the cache point separates them in the user message

Write unit tests covering: exact serialised output for a small project, blank-line collapsing, the 12,000-character cut, context-block stability across two calls, and context-block change after an ADR update or a new enabler is approved
Send ten draft requests to the real model with varied prompts and ADR selections; adjust the system prompt until all manual checklist items above pass consistently
